title: [VS Code/WSL] Capacity retries resume after reopening task; goal stalls for 10h41m and 58m

body:
### Summary

An unattended local Codex goal becomes stalled after `server_overloaded`. Automatic retries are recorded only much later, shortly after the task is reopened. This has now happened twice on 26 October 2026, including an overnight gap of 10 hours 41 minutes and a subsequent gap of 58 minutes. Reopening the task can restart a model attempt, but the goal itself remains blocked.

Please investigate durable background recovery separately from the original model-capacity rejection. A long-running goal should not silently depend on its conversation remaining rendered in the IDE.

### Environment

- Official Codex VS Code extension, version `26.1007.21434`.
- Windows VS Code with a WSL Linux workspace; both installed extension packages report that version.
- ChatGPT sign-in, built-in OpenAI provider.
- Failed goal turn selected `gpt-6.1-sol`, reasoning effort `max`.
- Exact bundled CLI version and account quota at the instant of failure were not independently checked. No claim is made that this was a quota exhaustion or an account restriction.

### Verified timeline

All times below are UTC, also local UK GMT on 26 October 2026.

| Time | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 02:42:05.680 | Goal continuation starts (`turn_trigger: goal`). |
| 02:47:47.793 | Turn completes with `error.codex_error_info: server_overloaded` and `Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.` |
| 13:29:04.276 | Extension logs record navigation/hydration of the affected thread; its prior state is `cold`, and its view is `mounted`. |
| 13:29:12.490 | Next recorded task start: `turn_trigger: capacity_retry_automatic`. No intervening turn starts appear in this thread's lifecycle records. |
| 13:35:08.503 | That retry completes with the same `server_overloaded` error. |
| 14:33:12.432 | Next recorded task start: `capacity_retry_automatic`, after the user reports reopening the task again. |

The first failure-to-next-start gap is **10h 41m 24.697s**; the second is **58m 03.929s**. These are observed task inactivity gaps, **not** measurements of how long OpenAI model capacity remained unavailable. Lower-level network retries that do not create task starts are not ruled out.

The read-only goal status after the first restart still reported `blocked`, with its last update corresponding to the overnight failure. A successful restart of a sampling attempt does not itself establish that unattended goal continuation has resumed.

### Installed retry-path observations

Read-only inspection of the installed extension's JavaScript found:

- A retry-delay sequence of `[10, 30, 120, 300]` seconds, followed by no further automatic delay for a qualifying consecutive failure sequence.
- The capacity retry countdown is created in a rendered chat component.
- Its interval uses `window.setInterval` inside a UI effect and is cleared when that effect is cleaned up.
- Retry eligibility also depends on a feature gate, thread readiness and the current session being the owner.

These observations and the reopen-to-retry correlation strongly suggest a recovery lifecycle gap when a task view is inactive/unmounted. They do **not** prove that view removal, the feature gate, owner state, or any single one of these conditions caused this occurrence; maintainers should correlate the internal event history.

No installed extension code, goal database, security setting, authentication data or retry setting was modified. No artificial user interaction or new parallel model probes were used to force recovery.

### Expected behaviour / investigation request

1. Persist a capacity-interrupted goal's pending retry independently of the chat view, within a documented bounded retry policy that respects server-requested delays.
2. Resume authorised goal work from its checkpoint when capacity returns, without requiring reopening the task or repeatedly reactivating a stalled goal.
3. Preserve intentional pauses, approval boundaries, account limits and cancellation; prevent concurrent duplicate turns or repeated side effects.
4. Show the last attempt, next scheduled attempt, retry exhaustion and whether the goal will actually continue unattended.
5. Test with an inactive/unmounted conversation, long background waits, repeated capacity errors and client restart.
6. Clarify whether this extension version has a known recovery defect and which released version fixes it, if applicable.

The user has experienced repeated disruption over a long-running development task and requests urgent investigation. The latest additional hour-long recurrence was checked against the timestamped lifecycle records above.

Related: #32020 (automatic retries for long-running goals) and #53569 (recurrent capacity errors).

Privacy: project contents, project name, local filesystem paths, account identity, raw logs and conversation/turn identifiers are deliberately omitted from this public report. A small private correlation set can be supplied through an official secure support channel.
